### Compass Pathways Completes COMP360 Psilocybin New Drug Application to U.S. FDA for Treatment-Resistant Depression


November 9, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s204.q4cdn.com/927483861/files/doc_news/Compass-Pathways-Completes-COMP360-Psilocybin-New-Drug-Application-to-U-S--FDA-for-Treatment-Resistant-Depression-2026.pdf)


- Robust NDA submission supported by data from two highly statistically significant Phase 3 trials and a Phase 2b study that each met its primary endpoint and involved a total of more than 1,000 participants living with highly chronic TRD
- Deep commercial capabilities in place to enable successful launch execution and broad patient access with launch readiness on track for expected launch in H12027, subject to FDA approval


LONDON & JERSEY CITY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Compass Pathways plc (Nasdaq: CMPS), a biotechnology company dedicated to unlocking urgently needed new treatment options in mental health care, today announced the Company completed its submission of a New Drug Application (NDA) to the U.S. FDA for COMP360 psilocybin, its investigational synthetic, proprietary formulation of psilocybin, for treatment-resistant depression (TRD).


"People living with treatment-resistant depression have gone too long experiencing disproportionate suffering, despite years of trying available treatment options without meaningful relief. The completion of our NDA submission reflects years of perseverance and commitment by patients, families, advocates, researchers and healthcare providers who have worked alongside us toward the shared goal of bringing new treatment options to this community,” said Kabir Nath, Chief Executive Officer of Compass Pathways. “Compass is leading the development of this new class of medicines with rigor and discipline, successfully completing the largest late-stage clinical program in psychedelic treatments. We are deeply grateful to the entire Compass team for the achievement of this extraordinary milestone. We look forward to continuing the review process, and we are focused on delivering COMP360 to patients as quickly as possible, subject to FDA approval. We have a world-class and fully scaled commercial organization, and the infrastructure and capabilities in place to support broad patient access upon approval.”


**About treatment-resistant depression (TRD)**


[TRD](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fpmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2Farticles%2FPMC10503923%2F&esheet=54637020&newsitemid=20261109020822&lan=en-US&anchor=TRD&index=1&md5=e9d2015d782978c1db87af4efdcfb9ae) is a form of[depression](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.who.int%2Fnews-room%2Ffact-sheets%2Fdetail%2Fdepression&esheet=54637020&newsitemid=20261109020822&lan=en-US&anchor=depression&index=2&md5=f9fa7fbc7f21d2c970afe3401c2c5538) , distinguished from[major depressive disorder](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2Fbooks%2FNBK559078%2F&esheet=54637020&newsitemid=20261109020822&lan=en-US&anchor=major+depressive+disorder&index=3&md5=53eb4ea2b4df40904086f091e8f2d5d1) (MDD), by its definition requiring an inadequate response to two or more courses of antidepressants of adequate dose and duration. An estimated 4 million people in the U.S. live with TRD, of whom fewer than 5% are currently on a TRD-indicated treatment.1,2,3 TRD has a significantly greater impact on individuals compared to MDD, leading to residual symptoms, poorer quality of life, increased comorbidities, higher mortality, and an increased risk of suicide.[5](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fpubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2F37713549%2F&esheet=54637020&newsitemid=20261109020822&lan=en-US&anchor=5&index=4&md5=fc982be1cf7c162a6079d95568bc3eb1) Research suggests this may be attributed to the role of altered brain network functioning in TRD, with biological changes becoming more entrenched with recurrent or prolonged depressive episodes.[4](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fpmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2Farticles%2FPMC13315732%2F&esheet=54637020&newsitemid=20261109020822&lan=en-US&anchor=4&index=5&md5=1ce565d14df42459a70ab25178ba8a8a) ,[5](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fpubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2F39232159%2F&esheet=54637020&newsitemid=20261109020822&lan=en-US&anchor=5&index=6&md5=b1236f125ae9c3cac2203f3bfa211002) ,[6](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fpubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2F39232159%2F&esheet=54637020&newsitemid=20261109020822&lan=en-US&anchor=6&index=7&md5=a036a0945875899d50867a226b46afe1) ,[7](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fpubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2F17074942%2F&esheet=54637020&newsitemid=20261109020822&lan=en-US&anchor=7&index=8&md5=c45a0e41b528554b9edf891d36214c5a) ,[8](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fpubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2F38240079%2F&esheet=54637020&newsitemid=20261109020822&lan=en-US&anchor=8&index=9&md5=a5687e549c351671f4274b0db36d0d69)


Many people living with TRD experience years of cycling through treatments that aren't providing meaningful relief, with an impact extending across work, school, relationships and daily life. A[national survey](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fassets.contentstack.io%2Fv3%2Fassets%2Fblta4f6f6922537743c%2Fblt88e0054b08f532b6%2FTRDSurvey_Report.pdf&esheet=54637020&newsitemid=20261109020822&lan=en-US&anchor=national+survey&index=10&md5=f043b4ac1c2a1eeb39044c87eb82581f) of people with TRD and their caregivers revealed the cumulative burden of the treatment cycle, with 95% of surveyed patients describing themselves as either functioning but struggling, surviving day-to-day or barely getting by. Furthermore, the impact extends well beyond the individual, with approximately 70% of caregivers reporting that TRD negatively affects the whole family's social, physical and/or mental health, reinforcing the urgent need for new treatment approaches that can meaningfully improve the lives of those affected by TRD.


**About Compass Pathways**


We believe mental health patients deserve the possibility of a better future. Compass Pathways plc (Nasdaq: CMPS) is a biotechnology company dedicated to unlocking urgently needed new treatment options in mental health care. Our initial focus is developing COMP360 psilocybin, a proprietary, investigational, synthetic psilocybin treatment under evaluation for treatment-resistant depression (TRD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). COMP360 is a potentially first-in-class treatment and has Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), as well as Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway (ILAP) designation in the UK for TRD. We are leading the world’s largest classic psychedelic clinical program in TRD, and building upon that robust foundation, we are executing a late-stage trial evaluating COMP360 for PTSD, another condition with high unmet need. Our goal is to advance treatments that move the field of psychiatry towards treatment options that offer rapid onset and sustained durability with infrequent dosing.


Compass is headquartered in London, UK, with a U.S. office in New Jersey.


We are driven by our purpose of unlocking pathways to be – opening futures filled with possibility. Together, we are on an ambitious journey toward enabling people living with mental health conditions to find clarity through self-discovery, because every journey needs a Compass.
